chunks: And by this chain from Bakr ibn Ishaq ibn Ammar from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, no one can fully appreciate the status of Allah; and just as no one can fully appreciate His status, so too no one can fully appreciate the status of His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family); and likewise, no one can fully appreciate the status of a believer. When he meets his brother and shakes hands with him, Allah looks at them both, and sins fall away from their faces until they separate, just as the strong wind shakes leaves off a tree.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward of shaking hands with a believing brother according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this hadith to illustrate the concept of *ta'zir* (divine attention) in interpersonal relations, where the mutual greeting of believers serves as a means of expiation for sins. The metaphor of wind shaking leaves emphasizes the sudden and complete removal of spiritual burdens, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on social cohesion (*mu'akhat*) as a form of worship. This interaction is not merely social but a spiritual transaction where divine gaze facilitates the shedding of faults.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. And from the previous chain from Bakr b. Ishaq b. Ammar from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said:

“One who is not aware of the status of Allah is not aware of the status of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.s.) also. And one who is not aware of the status of the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.s.) is not aware of the status of a believer also. If someone sees a believing brother and shakes hands with him, sins are wiped off from their faces like dry leaves fall off a tree due to wind, till they (the believers) separate from one another.”
